title: Word order 2
note: B1 repair after a1_word_order. English order is fixed: subject first, SVO, place before time at the end. Czech inversion is the error (Important for me is… / Very long was… / In Prague live… / This email sent Petr). Dummy it stays in b1_it_subject; clause openers out; fronted adverbials are not the target. Fronted time accepted as an alternate, not taught. Check: sort Correct/Needs repair then Quiz. No Type (cloze cannot force the subject). Quiz: which sentence is correct. Use: error-correction (use_mode: correct). Spec_Word-Order_B1_G_SS_2026-08-30 · rewrite 2026-08-30. · C57 recap card (You already know — Slovosled 1) added as card 1. · 2026-09-05 B1 loop: 21 -> 26 items, so the pack clears the 24-40 floor. Two Quiz distractors were correct English and both were also the Use prompt (B1/G4/E9): *I worked last year in Vienna* and *We met on Monday at the office* are things people say — time before place is a preference, not a rule, so a student who 'corrected' them was marked wrong for writing English. Both wrongs are now strings that cannot be said (*I last year worked…*, *We on Monday met…*), both time-first orders went into `accepts`, and the place-before-time card still teaches the neutral order. Items 5 and 11 were the same sentence with a different adjective — 11 is now *The film was really boring*. A4: *I drink coffee in the morning* demanded an article the Czech does not mark; the item is now *at work* and the pack is down to one A4 candidate (*at the office*, where English forces it). The five new items only drill classes the Common mistakes and Place-and-time cards already name (C11): object after the verb, adverb after the object, the actor first, time after the object, and no inversion after a fronted time phrase.
sort_rule: Subject first. A verb or a description at the front needs repair.

items.cz: Můj kolega včera poslal tu zprávu.

items.en: **We** moved to Brno two years ago.
items.cz: Před dvěma lety jsme se přestěhovali do Brna.

items.en: This problem solved **my team** last week.
items.cz: Tenhle problém vyřešil minulý týden můj tým.

quiz_options: English is important to me.
Important to me is English.
To me is important English.
accepts: English is important to me.
English is important for me.
items.explanation: The thing that is important is the subject: **English is**. Not *Important to me is English.
items.explanation_cz: Podmět je věc, která je důležitá: **English is**. Ne *Important to me is English.

quiz_options: I drink coffee at work.
Coffee I drink at work.
I at work drink coffee.
accepts: I drink coffee at work.
items.explanation: The object **coffee** sits after the verb. Czech *Kávu piju* puts the object first.
items.explanation_cz: Předmět **coffee** stojí za slovesem. Česky *Kávu piju* dává předmět dopředu.

quiz_options: Petr sent this email.
This email sent Petr.
Sent Petr this email.
accepts: Petr sent this email.
items.explanation: **Petr** did the sending, so **Petr** comes first. *This email sent Petr* makes the email the actor.
items.explanation_cz: **Petr** poslal ten e-mail, proto je **Petr** první. *This email sent Petr* z e-mailu dělá činitele.

quiz_options: Many people live in Prague.
In Prague live many people.
Live many people in Prague.
accepts: Many people live in Prague.
items.explanation: **Many people** is the subject. Place follows the verb: live **in Prague**.
items.explanation_cz: **Many people** je podmět. Místo jde za sloveso: live **in Prague**.

items.en: My team solved this problem last week.
items.cz: Tenhle problém vyřešil minulý týden můj tým.
quiz_options: My team solved this problem last week.
This problem solved my team last week.
Solved my team this problem last week.
accepts: My team solved this problem last week.
items.wrong: This problem solved my team last week.
items.explanation: **My team** solved it. The problem is the object, not the subject.
items.explanation_cz: Vyřešil to **my team**. Problém je předmět, ne podmět.

quiz_options: The meeting was very long.
Very long was the meeting.
Was very long the meeting.
accepts: The meeting was very long.
items.explanation: Descriptions follow **be**: **The meeting was** very long. Not *Very long was…
items.explanation_cz: Popis jde za **be**: **The meeting was** very long. Ne *Very long was…

items.en: I check my email every day.
quiz_options: I check my email every day.
I every day check my email.
Every day check I my email.
accepts: I check my email every day.
items.wrong: I every day check my email.
items.explanation: Do not put **every day** between subject and verb. **I check**, then the object, then the time.
items.explanation_cz: **every day** nestrkejte mezi podmět a sloveso. **I check**, pak předmět, pak čas.

items.en: I worked in Vienna last year.
quiz_options: I worked in Vienna last year.
I last year worked in Vienna.
In Vienna worked I last year.
accepts: I worked in Vienna last year.
I worked last year in Vienna.
items.wrong: I last year worked in Vienna.
items.explanation: Nothing goes between the subject and the verb: **I worked**. Place and time follow it — *in Vienna last year*.
items.explanation_cz: Mezi podmět a sloveso nepatří nic: **I worked**. Místo a čas jdou až za ně — *in Vienna last year*.

items.en: I like black coffee very much.
quiz_options: I like black coffee very much.
I like very much black coffee.
Very much I like black coffee.
accepts: I like black coffee very much.
I really like black coffee.
items.wrong: I like very much black coffee.
items.explanation: **like** + the object + **very much**. Not *like very much black coffee.
items.explanation_cz: **like** + předmět + **very much**. Ne *like very much black coffee.

items.en: Twenty people work in our office.
items.cz: V naší kanceláři pracuje dvacet lidí.
quiz_options: Twenty people work in our office.
In our office work twenty people.
Work twenty people in our office.
accepts: Twenty people work in our office.
items.wrong: In our office work twenty people.
items.explanation: **Twenty people** is the subject. Do not put the place before the subject.
items.explanation_cz: **Twenty people** je podmět. Místo nedejte před podmět.

items.en: Our boss signed this contract yesterday.
items.cz: Včera tu smlouvu podepsal náš šéf.
quiz_options: Our boss signed this contract yesterday.
This contract signed our boss yesterday.
Signed our boss this contract yesterday.
accepts: Our boss signed this contract yesterday.
Yesterday our boss signed this contract.
items.wrong: This contract signed our boss yesterday.
items.explanation: **Our boss** signed the contract. The contract is the object. *Yesterday our boss signed…* is also fine — the subject still comes next.
items.explanation_cz: **Our boss** smlouvu podepsal. Smlouva je předmět. *Yesterday our boss signed…* je taky v pořádku — podmět jde hned za tím.

quiz_options: The film was really boring.
Really boring was the film.
Was really boring the film.
accepts: The film was really boring.
items.explanation: **The film was** really boring. A description does not open the sentence, even when Czech puts it first.
items.explanation_cz: **The film was** really boring. Popis větu nezačíná, i když ho čeština dává dopředu.

items.en: We met at the office on Monday.
items.cz: V pondělí jsme se sešli v kanceláři.
quiz_options: We met at the office on Monday.
We on Monday met at the office.
On Monday met we at the office.
accepts: We met at the office on Monday.
We met on Monday at the office.
items.wrong: We on Monday met at the office.
items.explanation: **We met** stays together. The neutral end order is place then time: *at the office on Monday*.
items.explanation_cz: **We met** zůstává pohromadě. Neutrální pořadí na konci je místo, pak čas: *at the office on Monday*.

items.en: I read a book every evening.
quiz_options: I read a book every evening.
I read every evening a book.
A book I read every evening.
accepts: I read a book every evening.
items.wrong: I read every evening a book.
items.explanation: The object follows the verb: **read a book**. The time word goes after it, not between them.
items.explanation_cz: Předmět jde hned za sloveso: **read a book**. Časový výraz až za něj, ne mezi ně.

quiz_options: Petr speaks English very well.
Petr speaks very well English.
Very well Petr speaks English.
accepts: Petr speaks English very well.
items.explanation: **speaks English**, then **very well**. The adverb never splits the verb from its object.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív **speaks English**, pak **very well**. Příslovce nikdy nerozdělí sloveso a předmět.

quiz_options: Our neighbour broke this window.
This window broke our neighbour.
Broke our neighbour this window.
accepts: Our neighbour broke this window.
Our neighbor broke this window.
items.explanation: **Our neighbour** did it, so **Our neighbour** comes first. *This window broke our neighbour* makes the window the actor.
items.explanation_cz: Udělal to **our neighbour**, proto stojí první. *This window broke our neighbour* dělá činitele z okna.

items.en: We finished the project on Friday.
items.cz: Ten projekt jsme dokončili v pátek.
quiz_options: We finished the project on Friday.
We finished on Friday the project.
On Friday finished we the project.
accepts: We finished the project on Friday.
On Friday we finished the project.
items.wrong: We finished on Friday the project.
items.explanation: The time word goes after the object: **finished the project** on Friday. It cannot sit between the verb and the object.
items.explanation_cz: Časový výraz jde až za předmět: **finished the project** on Friday. Mezi sloveso a předmět nepatří.

items.en: Many students come here every year.
items.cz: Každý rok sem chodí mnoho studentů.
quiz_options: Many students come here every year.
Every year come here many students.
Come here many students every year.
accepts: Many students come here every year.
Every year many students come here.
items.wrong: Every year come here many students.
items.explanation: A time phrase at the front is fine, but the **subject** still comes next: *Every year many students come here*. English never swaps subject and verb here.
items.explanation_cz: Časový výraz na začátku je v pořádku, ale hned po něm musí přijít **podmět**: *Every year many students come here*. Angličtina tu podmět a sloveso nikdy neprohodí.

cards.title: Word order 2
points: Czech can move the same words.

cards.title: You already know
points: Place and time go at the end, **place** before **time**.
Word order 1 was the normal order. Here it moves, on purpose.

examples.en: We **have** English in Brno on Monday.
examples.cz: Máme angličtinu v Brně v pondělí.

cards.title: The subject comes first
points: A description after **be** does not open the sentence.

cards.title: Place and time
points: A time word first is fine if the **subject** is next.

cards.title: Order changes the meaning
points: Czech marks the actor with an ending.
